text:
Maya (AE): PulseHealth POC kickoff: customer wants 2.5h soak at sustained 650 qps, ~300-token outputs, p99 <190ms, errors <0.7%. They need a run plan, quick sizing, and an hourly cost delta for burst nodes + multi-az. Also asking for our SOC responses and a short acceptance checklist. Can SE/SRE + Solutions triage?
Diego (SE): Copy. Quick clarifications: what % streaming vs full responses and estimated cacheable prompt fraction? Also any required model family preference?
Maya (AE): ~50% streaming, ~45% repeatable prompts (good cache potential). They prefer the 13b family but are open to fallback.
Rohit (SRE): Initial infra rec: Dedicated pool with ~20% headroom -> size for ~780 qps. Autoscale min=1, max=3 nodes, cooldown 90s. Multi-AZ recommended for demo. Pre-warm KV cache during ramp. Fallback order should be 13b->7b for latency preservation. Recommend autoscale buffer to spin before scheduled surges if we know windows.
Diego (SE): Proposed load plan: warmup 15m, ramp 10m to 650 qps, steady 2.5h, cool-down 15m. Arrival: Poisson arrivals + periodic microbursts: every 30m a 45s spike at 3x to exercise tails. Models to test: rwd-13b-q4 (primary), rwd-13b-8k (if context matters), rwd-7b-q8 (fallback). Enable KV prefix caching and first-token streaming. Suggest initial max_batch_delay 7ms; reduce to 5ms if p99 misses.
Diego (SE): sample internal load command we use:
```
rwd-load --model rwd-13b-q4 --target-qps 650 --duration 9000 --ramp 600 --warmup 900 --burst-profile "every_30m:45s@3x" --concurrency 95 --payload-dist pulse_prompts.json
```
Lina (Solutions): Pricing quickballpark: Dedicated pool sized for rwd-13b-q4 to sustain 650 qps ~ $1,400/hr. For 2.5h + warmup/cooldown estimate ~ $3.6k. Multi-AZ + burst-ready extra node adds ~+15-20% hourly. Hosted token billing fallback estimate ~ $0.20 per 1k inferred tokens (very rough), will refine with actual token counts. I'll prepare two price lines: baseline and burst-ready.
load-bot: quick smoke run (internal):
```json
{"test":"pulse-smoke-2026-05-10","target_qps":650,"sustained_qps":645,"p50_ms":46,"p95_ms":128,"p99_ms":203,"error_rate_pct":0.6,"gpu_util_pct":85,"notes":"p99 203ms slightly above 190ms SLO. Try +20% capacity or lower max_batch_delay to 5ms. Consider KV pre-population to reduce tail from cold misses."}
```
Maya (AE): p99 203ms is close but above 190ms. Fastest wins to try before customer run?
Rohit (SRE): Easiest: spin +20% capacity and rerun a 30-45m validation. If still high, lower max_batch_delay to 5ms for this route (trade increased GPU ops). I can spin nodes now and schedule the validation in ~40m. Also will enable KV pre-warm during the ramp phase.
Diego (SE): I'll stage the config with lowered batch_delay as a fallback flag so we can flip quickly. Also will run a quick quality check on rwd-7b-q8 to ensure fallback meets PulseHealth quality bar.
Lina (Solutions): I'll package SOC redacted answers and the two pricing options into a short customer-facing PDF. Also adding a short acceptance checklist: sustained 650 qps for 2.5h, p99 <190ms, error rate <0.7%, KV cache hit >30% during steady, successful failover to fallback model without >1% request mutation.
load-bot: 30m validation after +20% capacity:
```json
{"test":"pulse-val-2026-05-10","target_qps":650,"sustained_qps":651,"p50_ms":42,"p95_ms":115,"p99_ms":186,"error_rate_pct":0.4,"gpu_util_pct":76,"notes":"p99 186ms meets <190ms SLO with +20% pool and KV pre-warm. Recommend final 2.5h soak with same config; monitor KV hit rate and streaming ratio."}
```
Maya (AE): Excellent  that's within acceptance. I'll propose two options to the customer: (A) baseline soak (B) soak + burst-ready (recommended). Scheduling the customer soak for next Tue. Thanks team! :rocket:
